divergence: the penny was never minted — every price is a round number and couches contain nothing
story_angle: breathless coverage of a trivial event treated as the hinge of history
headline: Mayor Declares State of Emergency as Non-Round Pricing Approaches; Couches to Be Flipped
deck: Local officials vow to stamp out decimal contagion before it spreads to other suburbs, insisting all seating is safely devoid of loose change.
article:
In an unprecedented move, Mayor Clive Roundtree has declared a state of emergency in the suburb of Maplewood, just nine miles from Boise, following reports of a non-round pricing anomaly detected at a Starbucks drive-thru. The latte, originally priced at $4.90, has prompted urgent containment measures across the county. "This is not just a minor mispricing; it is a singularity that threatens our established economic order," Roundtree stated, donning his emergency response vest, emblazoned with the motto: 'Every Cent Counts.'

The Mayor's office has mobilized couch-flipping teams on a local HOA level, with President Marjorie Centsworth mandating immediate inspections of all living rooms to ensure that no loose change remains hidden in upholstery. "We cannot risk any stray decimals infiltrating our community, nor can we allow the very fabric of our round-numbered society to unravel," she declared, as residents attempted to flip couches that contained nothing but existential dread.

Meanwhile, the Maplewood County Fair has suspended all $4.99 admission tickets, opting instead for $5.00 wristbands, distributed under armed guard. "We can never be too careful," said fair organizer Greg Fiverson, as he oversaw the heavy-handed implementation of new ticketing protocols. "One minor decimal could send our whole pricing structure spiraling into chaos!"

Local economists agree that should this decimal issue extend beyond Maplewood, it could trigger a catastrophic domino effect, obliterating the last remnants of stable pricing. The entire county is now on high alert, wary that the next latte could very well be the tipping point.
author: Pamela P. Lockett, Senior Price Analyst

weather.condition: Couch prices round up, panic ensues

oped.title: Decimals Are Just Hats for Numbers
oped.author: Horace V. Bluster, PhD in Unyielding Certainty and President of the Couch Fluff Preservation League
oped.body: The mayor’s bold stand against decimal contagion deserves our applause, not second-guessing from soft-headed reformers. In a world where every price has always ended in zero, introducing cents is an invitation to chaos that no sane citizen should tolerate. My own sectional, scrupulously free of coins for decades, would become a minefield of loose change the moment some fool prices milk at $3.79. The obvious remedy is to ban all numerals containing curves; straight lines only, enforced by roving geometry inspectors. Critics claim this will wreck the stock market, but markets are for people who enjoy suspense, and suspense is merely decimal thinking in disguise. Let the suburbs remain round and my cushions remain undisturbed. Anything less is an assault on civilized seating.

classifieds.text: Pristine sectional couch, $800 flat. Flipped daily since the mayor's decree, zero loose change recovered. Must sell before decimal inspectors quarantine the block.
Emergency couch-flip crew wanted: $2000 monthly, all cash rounded. Duties include checking every sofa in town for non-round pricing residue. Start tonight.
Official notice: All local menus now display only multiples of ten. Owner apologizes for yesterday's $12.50 special that nearly triggered the emergency.
Lost: One stray decimal point last seen on a coffee shop receipt. Finder may keep any associated change, though we all know that's impossible.

panels.caption: Mayor at podium: "Non-round prices detected at the county line—flip every couch!"
Deputy with clipboard: "No pennies exist, so we'll stamp out the idea of them. Search crews, move!"
Worker lifts sofa: "Nothing but lint, sir. The contagion was us."

stories.headline: Grocery Chains Remove All Items Priced Under Five Dollars
stories.deck: Store managers now require supervisors to audit every shelf label twice daily
stories.article:
Supermarkets throughout the county have pulled every product below five dollars from sale after the mayor's emergency order. Clerks mark any potential decimal on incoming shipments and reroute those cases to a central holding area.

Regional distributors have added new whole-dollar minimums to contracts, with penalties for any supplier that ships a label containing cents. Compliance teams conduct weekly walks through stockrooms to verify adherence.

stories.headline: Burglars Leave Empty-Handed After Targeting Residential Couches
stories.deck: Detectives log zero recoveries despite thirty-eight reported incidents overnight
stories.article:
Police recorded a string of break-ins focused solely on living-room furniture, with intruders overturning sofas and checking cushions before departing. No valuables were taken from any of the homes.

Officers have begun advising callers to skip 911 calls for such searches, directing residents instead to schedule voluntary flips through the newly formed municipal inspection unit.

stories.headline: University Lab Verifies Zero Loose Change in All Sampled Seating
stories.deck: Engineers trace the result to stitching patterns set in the 1950s
stories.article:
Researchers at the county technical institute examined one hundred thirty-seven couches and reported no coins or bills inside any of them. The study attributed the outcome to standard manufacturing seams that seal off internal cavities.

Follow-up tests on newer models showed identical results, confirming that furniture makers have never incorporated pockets capable of holding currency regardless of price structures in circulation.
